$comment: G01 tool/state contract. Normative machine-readable source of truth for the Miliastra business tool surface. Downstream implementers (T03, T05, T06, T08, and through T05/T06 also T09, T10) MUST implement these enums verbatim. Validated by ./validate.py.

authority.note: Every value below is derived from a file that exists on disk. Nothing here is invented; where the plan text and the code disagree, the disagreement is recorded under conflicts[] and resolved explicitly.

operationState.description: Lifecycle state of ONE business operation, identified by operationId, as observable on disk. This is the vocabulary T06's business ledger stores.

discriminator.description: The single rule that separates claimed from dispatched. It is already implemented by the native CLI and is quoted verbatim: scene_cli.py:685-694 computes possibly_started = bool(run_path and any((Path(run_path)/name).exists() for name in ('direct-launch-intent.json', 'launch.claim', 'attempt.used'))) and then result['outcomeUncertain'] |= possibly_started. The business layer must use the same three file names plus two journal-level names, and must never infer 'claimed' from the absence of a reply.
discriminator.rule: evidence present -> dispatched; evidence absent AND a claim exists -> claimed; no claim at all -> never-claimed

rules.rule: A claim is written before any dispatch, atomically, and is never deleted. Evidence: author.py:229-241 (directory.mkdir() is the atomic claim, exclusive_json writes claim.json with the command fingerprint).

A mutation whose state is claimed, dispatched or outcome-unknown is NEVER re-dispatched, neither with the same operationId nor with a new one, until it has been reconciled from the original receipt. Evidence: author.py:238 raises 'REQUEST_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; inspect evidence; no retry'; T06.md:64 '不换 ID 重试'.

rejected may only be produced while no dispatch evidence exists. A refusal after the dispatch boundary is a contract violation. Evidence: author.py:74-83 refusal() pins outcomeUncertain=False and is only reachable before the journal directory exists; author.py:213-223 comment 'a rejected build must leave no trace to reconcile later'.

outcome-unknown is never a euphemism for claimed. If the system cannot tell whether the request left the process, the honest value is dispatched/outcome-unknown, never claimed. Anti-pattern on disk: entity_server.py:568-578 maps 'a claim exists' and 'no claim exists' onto two different labels, but maps 'claim exists without result' onto a single hard-coded string and never checks the dispatch evidence.

The transition to a terminal state happens exactly once, when result.json is published. A late receipt attaches to the operation that produced it, never to a newer one. Evidence: author.py:261 exclusive_json(directory/'result.json', ...) - the exclusive create is the publication event; T03.md:75 '迟到回执 ... 写入原 operation 证据，不激活旧实例'.

reconcileState.description: T06.md:42 uses known-success/known-failure/unknown. That is a PROJECTION of operationState, not a second truth. Implement it as a total function so the two can never disagree.
reconcileState.rule: The projection is many-to-one and lossy in one direction only: reconcileState must never be persisted as the authoritative value; operationState is. Evidence: T06.md:42 (never infer never-written from not-seen).

businessState.description: The model-facing verdict. This is the field named state in the tool result. Closed set fixed by TOOL-CONTRACT.md:48-52 and T05.md:37.

rules.rule: state is the only business verdict. ok and isError are transport-level. Required: ok === (state === 'completed') and result.isError === (state !== 'completed'). Generator counterexample on disk: entity_server.py:487-495 returns _ok(...) with isError false, created false and liveReadback fail, i.e. a transport success carrying a business failure. G01.md:46 names this exact case.

Any success-shaped boolean the tool returns (created, saved, deleted, placed) is derived from state and from counted evidence, never computed independently. created === true requires state === 'completed'.
T06.md:42's known-success/known-failure/unknown is reconcileState, not state. Do not emit three vocabularies in one object.

stages.description: Per-tool-call stage reporting. Separately resolved, separately reported. The set is fixed by TOOL-CONTRACT.md:32-37 and T05.md:38.

statusValueNotes.not-run: this tool call does not perform this stage. MUST carry a reason. NEVER means fail.
statusValueNotes.pass: the stage completed and is backed by at least one evidenceRef.
statusValueNotes.fail: the stage ran and did not meet its own criterion. MUST carry at least one evidenceRef and a reason.
statusValueNotes.blocked: the stage cannot proceed for a named external reason. MUST carry reason.
statusValueNotes.unknown: the stage was attempted and its outcome could not be established. MUST carry reason. This is the correct value when the evidence is unreadable, not not-run.
statusValueNotes.not-applicable: the stage can never apply to this capability. MUST carry reason, and is forbidden for any item the 07 checklist marks required.

stages.aliasRule: persistence is accepted as an input alias for one contract version and MUST NOT be emitted: TOOL-CONTRACT.md:55 '新接口统一使用 stages.saveDiff；旧 persistence 只在 T05 兼容迁移层映射，不并行维护成功真相'. The literal token 'failed' is never a valid status; the token is 'fail'.

stageLocality.rule: A pass in one stage is evidence for that stage only and for no other. liveReadback pass never implies saveDiff pass; saveDiff pass never implies reopen pass; reopen pass never implies runtime pass. Evidence: entity_server.py:22-27 docstring states this as the reason the five fields exist separately; TOOL-CONTRACT.md:57 '创建数量+1不等于模板/属性验收'.
stageLocality.enforcement: Each stage object MUST carry its own evidenceRef array. A result with stages.<x>.status === 'pass' and an empty evidenceRef is invalid and must be refused before publication (T05.md:43, T05.md:76 '缺字段 ... 拒绝发布结果').

stageApplicability.note: Which tool may assert which stage, given the layer it actually drives. Anything else is not-run with a reason.

saveDiffRule.rule: nativeStatus === 0 is an execution fact, not a saveDiff pass. Required: saveDiff.status === 'pass' only when the formal-file differential meets the G02 rule set. Counterexample on disk: .runtime/authoring/requests/mcpsave1790669923/result.json has backend.nativeStatus 0, backend.persistenceVerified false and backend.gilChanged {'1073741839': true}, while backend/entity_server.py:549-551 reports persistence status 'pass' with detail 'native save status 0 on the target level'. G01.md:47 names this exact case.

taskStages.description: The task-run-record stage set, distinct from the tool-call stage set. Used by .runtime/cordis-plan-work/<taskId>/<run>/result.json.
taskStages.relationship: stages (tool) is a strict subset of taskStages (task). source/offline/loader/mcp/aiToolCall are pipeline stages that no single business tool call can assert; a tool must never claim them.

notes.none: state completed; nothing further for this operation
notes.fix-input: a pre-dispatch refusal; correct the input or the prerequisite and submit a NEW operationId
notes.poll-same-operation: state pending; query the SAME operationId; never dispatch
notes.reconcile: state unknown; read the original receipt; never dispatch
notes.report-and-repair: state failed; use changed[] and failedItems[] to plan a bounded repair
notes.await-human: the execution layer is unavailable or blocked; a human must act. This is the only value a tool may use to ask for elevation.

nextAction.freeTextRule: nextAction MUST be one of these tokens. Free-text guidance goes to nextActionDetail. Counterexample on disk: .runtime/cordis-plan-work/G01/20260929T154241270706Z-0f8890b09662400eaa225cbda072402d/result.json carries nextAction 'Read dispatch.md and verify prerequisites with the coordinator.'

idempotency.description: The exact rules implemented by tools/authoring/author.py:209-262, verified offline by the G01 harness (see the decision record). The business layer must not weaken or duplicate them.
idempotency.keyShapeSource: author.py:211 and author.py:432; backend/entity_server.py:156-159 checks the same shape with a 1..80 bound.

fingerprint.definition: sha256 over the canonical JSON encoding of the WHOLE bound command, not over business parameters alone.
fingerprint.consequence: Replaying an operation with a freshly derived review produces a different review path, therefore a different fingerprint, therefore REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT instead of a replay.

rules.rule: same operationId + same bound command -> replay the original receipt, dispatch nothing.
same operationId + different bound command -> refuse, dispatch nothing.
claim present, result absent -> outcome unknown, dispatch nothing, retry forbidden.
rules.observed: author.py:236-238 raises ValueError('REQUEST_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; inspect evidence; no retry')

rules.rule: journal directory present, claim absent -> REQUEST_INCOMPLETE_CLAIM; no retry.

The business layer MUST resolve idempotency BEFORE deriving any baseline, backup or review. Order: (1) look up the business ledger by operationId; (2) if a claim exists, return its state and dispatch nothing; (3) only if the id was never claimed may baseline/backup/review be produced and a dispatch be attempted. Deriving a review before the lookup turns a legitimate replay into REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT.
rules.evidence: author.py:227-239 combined with author.py:347-349 ('Supplied paths are part of the command, so the journal fingerprint binds them: replaying the same request id with a different session, review or baseline is a conflict, not a replay').
rules.defectOnDisk: backend/entity_server.py:480-486 calls derive_review() before dispatch_write(); a second identical call therefore derives a second review and is refused instead of replaying. T05/T06 must fix the order.

rules.rule: Non-finite numbers are rejected before the fingerprint is even computable (allow_nan=False). NaN and Infinity can never reach the native layer through this path.
rules.observed: author.py:92 and author.py:415-417 (scale must be strictly positive); backend/entity_server.py:211-216 rejects non-finite components as TRANSFORM_INVALID

rules.rule: A read (mutating false) that fails never enters the mutation lane: outcomeUncertain is computed as `command['mutating'] and backend.outcomeUncertain` and is therefore false for a read even when the transport died. Verified offline, and cross-checked against .runtime/authoring/requests/author-live-lookup-01/result.json which reads '"ok": false, "outcomeUncertain": false' at top level while its backend carries 'BRIDGE_TRANSPORT_FAILED'.

retryAttempted is always reported and is always false. No layer in this project retries automatically. Evidence: every result.json in .runtime/authoring/requests/ carries retryAttempted false; author.py:250, author.py:259, elevated-request.py:89, elevated-request.py:96, elevated-runner check comments.

The queue has a SECOND, independent idempotency key one layer down: the 32-hex queueRequestId. Its permanent marker <rid>.submission.json is never deleted, so a re-send with identical bytes only polls and a re-send with different bytes raises QUEUE_REQUEST_ID_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH. That key is execution-layer and must never appear in a tool argument.
rules.observed: elevated-request.py:103-122; comment at :106-107 'Reusing an ID with different contents is an error, never a second dispatch.'

boundary.description: What a tool call may carry and what it must never carry, because the helper owns execution.
boundary.principle: The model supplies business parameters and opaque handles that this project minted. Everything that selects WHAT RUNS belongs to the execution layer. Evidence: backend/entity_server.py:14-20 and :113-114; docs/entity-create/MCP-BUSINESS-CONTRACT.md:19-23.

closedSchemaIsTheMechanism.runnerComment: elevated-runner.ps1:410-411 'Closed schema. The action selects exactly which fields exist, so hash, exe, run, wrapper, plan and baseline paths are not merely unused but unrepresentable.'

knownGaps: The runner's `fs`, `load` and `status` request kinds have NO closed field set: extra keys are accepted and silently ignored (elevated-runner.ps1:783-802, :804-816; elevated-fs-ops.ps1:83-285). No business tool reaches those kinds today; if one ever does, a closed schema must be added first.
Grep shows no mutex or single-instance lock in elevated-runner.ps1. Two helpers against one queue directory are not prevented by the runner. The queue carries no `timeout` field at any point.

The runner's native-scene action set is a FOURTH copy of a whitelist (with elevated-request.py:238, build_scene_profile.py TEMPLATES and OwnedEntityDelete.cs), and all of them are compared as exact sets. A tool that advertises a capability must not be the authority for whether the native layer will accept it.

errorTaxonomy.description: Closed taxonomy of the codes this tool surface may emit, each with the phase in which it may be produced. A code that appears outside this table is a contract violation.

disposition.rule: disposition is determined by WHERE the code is raised, not by the code alone. A code whose disposition is context-dependent MUST be resolved by its emitting call site; the emitter supplies phase explicitly. This is the rule that a single catch-all code cannot satisfy.
disposition.contextDependentRows: Exactly three codes in codes[] have disposition null and contextDependent true, and they are the only three allowed to appear on both sides of the boundary: READBACK_FAILED, READBACK_WRONG_LEVEL and READBACK_NOT_ACCEPTED. A contextDependent row lists its permitted values in allowedDispositions, and the emitter must pick one of them and report the phase. Every other row's disposition is fixed and may not be overridden by an emitter.
disposition.antiPattern: backend/entity_server.py:138-149 _fail() produces one shape with every stage not-run and no phase, for both pre-dispatch and post-dispatch failures. A post-write readback failure (entity_server.py:497) is therefore reported as if nothing had happened. _fail() must be split into _refuse() and _unknown().

upstreamPassthrough.rule: Codes from the ledger, queue, runner and native layers are carried inside error.upstream = {layer, code, message}, and are NEVER the top-level error.code. The top-level code is always from the table below.

registration.description: Who registers what, and where the refusal happens. G01.md:24 step 7 and step 8.

mcpPassthrough.consequence: The Miliastra Cordis plugin MUST NOT re-register any mw_* tool. Doing so either collides on the public name or produces a second, drifting description of the same capability. The seven current tools publish as mcp__miliastra__mw_scene_<name>.

lifecycle.description: Plugin unload, cancellation and in-flight operations. G01.md:23 step 6.

rules.rule: Unloading the plugin removes tools, listeners and its own MCP child process. It never stops, restarts or disconnects the game, the editor or the resident helper. Evidence: EXECUTION-CONTRACT.md:49.

Cancelling a wait is not a rollback. The operation keeps its state and its ledger. A cancelled operation with no dispatch evidence may be reported rejected/CANCELLED_BEFORE_DISPATCH; with dispatch evidence it is pending or unknown. Evidence: T03.md:40, :74; EXECUTION-CONTRACT.md:50.

A new plugin instance never re-dispatches a request left over from a previous instance, and never reuses an old request as if it were a new call. It queries the original operation. Evidence: T03.md:76; EXECUTION-CONTRACT.md:50.
Unload leaves operationId, caseId and the ledger location for reconciliation. Journals, evidence and recovery copies are never deleted. Evidence: T03.md:42.
The tool must never claim a rollback it did not perform, and must never report a reduction in side effect because the caller stopped waiting.

Each entry asserts that the literal string appears in the named file. validate.py --citations recomputes this against the working tree; a failure means a decision in this contract has lost its evidence and must be re-derived, not re-asserted.

conflicts.resolution: Canonical key is saveDiff; persistence is an accepted INPUT alias for one contract version and is never emitted.

conflicts.otherText: TOOL-CONTRACT.md:54 and T05.md:38 list fail (plus blocked and not-applicable).
conflicts.resolution: Closed set is not-run/pass/fail/blocked/unknown/not-applicable. The token failed is invalid; it is accepted as an input alias only.

conflicts.planText: T05.md:43 and T08.md:38 say evidenceRef / evidenceRefs.
conflicts.resolution: Different artifacts. A tool-result stage carries evidenceRef (plus evidenceSha256); a task run record keeps the plan template's evidence array, which validate_plan.py reads. Mapping: taskRecord.stages[x].evidence is the union of the toolResult evidenceRef values for that stage.

conflicts.otherText: T08.md:39 lists 11 (5 plus source/offline/loader/cli/mcp/aiToolCall); RESULT.json defines 10 with no cli.
conflicts.resolution: Two sets by design: tool-call stages (5) and task-run stages (10, from RESULT.json which validate_plan.py validates). cli has no counterpart in the validated template and is an open item owned by T08 - see openItems.

conflicts.otherText: T06.md:42 defines known-success/known-failure/unknown; prepare_task.py writes state 'prepared' into the same-named key; CASE.json uses verdict.
conflicts.resolution: Three namespaces, one truth. operationState is authoritative and persisted; businessState is the model-facing projection; reconcileState is T06's read-time projection. The task run record's state/verdict is a FOURTH namespace belonging to the plan tooling and must not be reused for a business operation.

conflicts.otherText: registry.json, RESULT.json, CASE.json and native review records use the integer schemaVersion 1.
conflicts.resolution: contractVersion is a string ("1"); schemaVersion is an integer (1). They version different things and must not be conflated. A tool result carries contractVersion; a persisted record carries schemaVersion.

openItems.detail: T08.md:39 lists an 11th task stage cli that docs/cordis-plan/templates/RESULT.json does not define. Owner: T08. Resolution: either emit the RESULT.json ten and file CLI-level evidence under offline, or raise a plan change against the template. Do not silently add an eleventh key, because validate_plan.py validates the template rather than the instance.

The on-disk parameter name is levelHandle (backend/entity_server.py:440,459,522,587). G01.md:25 and TOOL-CONTRACT.md:11 name the concept targetHandle. Owner: T05. backend/entity_server.py:587 requires the caller to supply a bridge runId. G01.md:25 forbids the model from assembling a bridge runId. Owner: T10 with T06. The server must resolve the current bridge run the same way it resolves the elevated queue, and return CLEANUP_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE when none is live.
